title: D. Nene and the Mex Operator

legend: Nene gave you an array of integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ0%% of length n%%ZSMJ1%%.
You can perform the following operation no more than 5⋅105%%ZSMJ2%% times (possibly zero):
Choose two integers l%%ZSMJ3%% and r%%ZSMJ4%% such that 1≤l≤r≤n%%ZSMJ5%%, compute x%%ZSMJ6%% as MEX({al,al+1,…,ar})%%ZSMJ7%%, and simultaneously set al:=x,al+1:=x,…,ar:=x%%ZSMJ8%%.
Here, MEX%%ZSMJ9%% of a set of integers {c1,c2,…,ck}%%ZSMJ10%% is defined as the smallest non-negative integer m%%ZSMJ11%% which does not occur in the set c%%ZSMJ12%%.

Your goal is to maximize the sum of the elements of the array a%%ZSMJ13%%. Find the maximum sum and construct a sequence of operations that achieves this sum. Note that you don't need to minimize the number of operations in this sequence, you only should use no more than 5⋅105%%ZSMJ14%% operations in your solution.
input: The first line contains an integer n%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤n≤18%%ZSMJ16%%) — the length of the array a%%ZSMJ17%%.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ18%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ19%% (0≤ai≤107%%ZSMJ20%%) — the array a%%ZSMJ21%%.
output: In the first line, output two integers s%%ZSMJ22%% and m%%ZSMJ23%% (0≤m≤5⋅105%%ZSMJ24%%) — the maximum sum of elements of the array a%%ZSMJ25%% and the number of operations in your solution.
In the i%%ZSMJ26%%-th of the following m%%ZSMJ27%% lines, output two integers l%%ZSMJ28%% and r%%ZSMJ29%% (1≤l≤r≤n%%ZSMJ30%%), representing the parameters of the i%%ZSMJ31%%-th operation.
It can be shown that the maximum sum of elements of the array a%%ZSMJ32%% can always be obtained in no more than 5⋅105%%ZSMJ33%% operations.
note: In the first example, after the operation with l=1%%ZSMJ34%% and r=2%%ZSMJ35%% the array a%%ZSMJ36%% becomes equal to [2,2]%%ZSMJ37%%. It can be shown that it is impossible to achieve a larger sum of the elements of a%%ZSMJ38%%, so the answer is 4%%ZSMJ39%%.
In the second example, the initial sum of elements is 13%%ZSMJ40%% which can be shown to be the largest.
In the third example, the array a%%ZSMJ41%% changes as follows:
after the first operation (l=3%%ZSMJ42%%, r=3%%ZSMJ43%%), the array a%%ZSMJ44%% becomes equal to [1,100,0,1]%%ZSMJ45%%;
after the second operation (l=3%%ZSMJ46%%, r=4%%ZSMJ47%%), the array a%%ZSMJ48%% becomes equal to [1,100,2,2]%%ZSMJ49%%.
It can be shown that it is impossible to achieve a larger sum of the elements of a%%ZSMJ50%%, so the answer is 105%%ZSMJ51%%.
